doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Segregated Memphis clubs and the dance-blues repertoire
summary: Clubs were segregated in 1950-52; the repertoire included The Hucklebuck, Night Train and slow blues with vocalists.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I see. Were the clubs segregated at that time?
Yes. The clubs were segregated at the time but there were a couple of artists [who] would be able to come in, but for the most part all the clubs were segregated, yeah.
And this would have been around 19 —
So your repertoire of blues would include tunes like “The Hucklebuck.”
“Night Train,” “The Boogie Woogie,” a lot of slow blues with the singing, with the vocalist singing and stuff like that.
